title: Granular reserve buckets and scaling orchestration PRD
creator: Marco Ruiz
background: Large tenants and platform teams require more predictable behaviour when reserved capacity is partially used, during transient bursts, and when autoscaling events occur. Current reserved-pool behavior is coarse: a tenant either consumes reserved slots or is routed to fallback, which causes inefficient capacity utilization and sudden performance changes for customer workloads.
problem_statement: We need a mechanism to subdivide tenant reservations into multiple 'reserve buckets' with configurable elasticity credits and an orchestration policy that coordinates autoscale, prewarm, and graceful evacuation to improve utilization while maintaining isolation guarantees and predictable SLOs.
goals: Allow product teams to create multiple reserve buckets per tenant with independent size, priority, and burstable credit rules
Introduce an orchestration layer that coordinates autoscale decisions, prewarm actions, and cross-bucket fallback to preserve latency SLOs during contention
Reduce steady-state unused reserved capacity by >= 20% via better sharing and controlled borrowing between buckets
Provide console and API controls for configuring bucket policies, credit decay, and emergency evacuation thresholds
Ship acceptance criteria and monitoring that enable safe progressive rollout and rollback
success_metrics: Reserved capacity utilization increase: +20% within 8 weeks of rollout
Reduction in 'sudden fallback' incidents for top 50 tenants by 40%
No regressions in p95 latency for reserved requests during controlled experiments
Number of tenant-configured buckets in production (target: 50 tenants)
non_goals: Full multitenant market-wide shared pools (this is focused on per-tenant reserve subdivisions)
Replacing global scheduling or completely changing the kernel selection logic
On-prem private control plane changes outside the agent and config model
assumptions: Serving runtime can expose a real-time slot accounting endpoint for bucket allocations (ENG dependency)
KV cache behavior is unaffected by bucket-level routing decisions
Autoscaler can accept weighted prewarm requests and throttle them during cluster pressure
stakeholders: Eng: Serving runtime team (owner: Linnea Carlson)
SRE: Capacity and autoscale (owner: Kofi Mensah)
Design/Console: UX for bucket config (owner: Priya Desai)
Sales/CS: Early access coordination (owner: Jenna Bloom)
requirements: Config model: API and Console support for creating up to N buckets per tenant with fields: name, base_reserve, burst_credit, priority_weight, credit_decay_seconds, emergency_evacuate_threshold
Credit ledger: lightweight per-tenant ledger for tracking earned/consumed burst credits with linear decay and audit logs
Orchestration policy: policy engine that uses bucket weights + credits + cluster pressure signals to decide prewarm, autoscale, and cross-borrow actions
Fallback rules: define deterministic fallback order across buckets and to public fallback models when all buckets exhausted
SLA enforcement: ability to pin a bucket to a strict non-preemptible class (for highest-tier customers)
Observability: dashboards for bucket utilization, credit burn rate, fallback events, and related latency breakdowns
API: idempotent endpoints to modify bucket config, query current credits, and force-evacuate a bucket
Telemetry: structured logs and traces that include bucket_id for every reserved request
api_spec: POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/buckets - create bucket - payload: {name, base_reserve, burst_credit, priority_weight, credit_decay_seconds}
GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/buckets/{bucket_id}/credits - returns current credit balance and burn history
POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/buckets/{bucket_id}:evacuate - triggers graceful drain of in-flight requests and prevents new allocations until released
console_changes: New 'Reserve Buckets' tab on tenant page showing bucket list, utilization sparkline, credit balance, and actions (edit, evacuate, pin)
Bucket creation modal with guided defaults and recommended policies based on historical traffic
Visualization of orchestration decisions (why a prewarm or fallback occurred) in the request trace pane
RBAC: restrict bucket management to tenant admins and platform operators
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags and backend API only; enable for internal tenants and SRE experiments
Phase 1: Beta with 5 pilot customers; collect telemetry and iterate policies (2-4 weeks)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50 tenants behind default safe policy with monitoring thresholds for rollback
Phase 3: Open to all tenants with migration guide and recommended defaults
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert if average credit burn rate across all buckets exceeds historical baseline by +150%
SLO dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency for reserved vs fallback paths with bucket filter
Alert on unexpected preemption: >3 evacuations in 1h for a tenant
Runbook: steps to pause bucket borrowing and force-evacuate buckets during cluster emergency
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: create, update, list buckets via API and Console and verify persistence
Credit ledger correctness: credits accrue and decay per configured rules with auditable events
Orchestration logic: under simulated contention, higher-priority buckets maintain their base_reserve while lower-priority buckets borrow only up to configured burst_credit
Evacuation: evacuate API drains in-flight requests gracefully within configurable timeout and prevents new allocations
Observability: dashboards populate within 5 minutes of enabling feature and fallback events include bucket_id in logs
No regression: p95 latency for reserved requests remains within 5% of baseline in controlled experiments
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive borrowing could starve critical tenants - Mitigation: conservative defaults and automatic cap on per-tenant borrow percentage
Risk: Complexity in orchestration leads to hard-to-debug decisions - Mitigation: decision audit log + synthetic workload simulator for SRE
Risk: Bookkeeping overhead impacts runtime latency - Mitigation: implement ledger as eventual-consistent in-memory structure with periodic durable snapshots
Risk: Tenant misconfiguration causes increased costs - Mitigation: console guardrails and cost-estimate preview when creating buckets
open_questions: What is a safe default for credit_decay_seconds for general web-app workloads? (SRE guidance required)
Should emergency_evacuate_threshold be absolute cluster pressure metric or relative to tenant historic usage?
Do we allow cross-tenant borrowing in constrained zones as a last-resort emergency feature?
What billing implications exist when a tenant borrows capacity from another bucket within the same tenant?
